title: "refine the runner config page in general settings ![18849.png](assets/18849.png) There's a few obvious issues such as : - the whole box should be clickable not just the runners name - it should auto populated fields even if just left on defaults (namely the file addresses) - the model selection should not just be a text box but should be able to toggle the models aytodetected by the runner.  - there should be a button to manually rekickoff model detection.  - the runner should be able to be updated from this page  There are other need for refinement so don't take this as a complete list just starting points. Do your own refinement"

# Goal
# refine the runner config page in general settings

![18849.png](assets/18849.png)

There's a few obvious issues such as :
- the whole box should be clickable not just the runners name
- it should auto populated fields even if just left on defaults (namely the file addresses)
- the model selection should not just be a text box but should be able to toggle the models aytodetected by the runner. 
- there should be a button to manually rekickoff model detection. 
- the runner should be able to be updated from this page 

There are other need for refinement so don't take this as a complete list just starting points. Do your own refinement

setup\"})","meta":{"toolName":"bash","toolCallId":"call_01a1a31508f07093bbcdc843292a9869","args":"{\"command\":\"sed -n 1,80p canary-e2e/playwright.config.js 2>&1; echo ===; sed -n 1,60p canary-e2e/tests/urls.js 2>&1\",\"description\":\"Check canary stack provisioning setup\"}","output":"// Canary suite target selection.\n\nconst { execFileSync } = require(\"node:child_process\");\nconst fs = require(\"node:fs\");\nconst path = require(\"node:path\");\n\n// CANARY_BASE_URL / CANARY_API_URL (both, verbatim): the suite drives the\n// operator-provided stack, exactly as documented in tests/urls.js — for\n// pointing the suite at an already-running dev/scratch stack the operator\n// owns.\n//\n// Both UNSET (the default): the suite PROVISIONS ITS OWN throwaway stack on\n// dedicated scratch ports — API on :3399 with a scratch PROJECTS_ROOT, vite\n// on :5299 with the browser wired to that API via VITE_API_BASE/VITE_WS_URL.\n// This keeps a bare `npx playwright test` / `npm run test:canary` from ever\n// accidentally driving a LIVE deployment that may be listening on the dev\n// defaults (:3100/:5173) — the suite must never mutate a backend it does not\n// own (the 2026-09-11 quick-review incident ran the whole suite against the\n// production API and produced false regressions: axe colour-contrast on the\n// RUNNING badge, workflow-switch/task-card state pollution, and tasks\n// executed by the production engine).\n//\n// The scratch API also runs with KAINBAIN_DISABLE_SCHEDULER: the autonomous\n// scheduler (started unconditionally by api/index.js) re-dispatches every\n// in_stage task sitting in an automated stage within one tick (3s), which\n// silently completed the suites' deliberately passive fixtures (footer-\n// overlay's \"Inspector overlap e2e\", task-lifecycle, mobile-responsive card\n// fixtures) and made card-visibility assertions race against task\n// completion. The specs' standing premise — \"/compute/stop keeps the\n// dispatcher off; tests drive stages explicitly\" — only holds with the\n// scheduler disabled (config.js documents this env var for exactly \"test\n// harnesses or scratch instances\"). Explicit execute:true and engine-driven\n// flows are unaffected.\n//\n// Exactly one of the two set: a configuration error. Splitting the pair\n// silently mixes an operator-owned half with a defaulted half (e.g. browser\n// talking to :3100 while the suite thinks it drives a scratch API), which is\n// precisely the ambiguity this split exists to remove — fail fast instead.\nconst operatorBaseURL = process.env.CANARY_BASE_URL;\nconst operatorApiURL = process.env.CANARY_API_URL;\nconst usesOperatorStack = Boolean(operatorBaseURL && operatorApiURL);\nif (!usesOperatorStack && (operatorBaseURL || operatorApiURL)) {\n\tthrow new Error(\n\t\t\"canary-e2e: set BOTH CANARY_BASE_URL and CANARY_API_URL to drive a specific stack, or neither to auto-provision an isolated scratch stack (API :3399 + vite :5299).\",\n\t);\n}\n\nconst baseURL = usesOperatorStack ? operatorBaseURL : \"http://localhost:5299\";\nconst apiURL = usesOperatorStack ? operatorApiURL : \"http://localhost:3399\";\n\n// Host-wide canary mutex (canary-lock.js): exactly one suite may own the\n// fixed scratch ports at a time, or overlapping suites kill each other's\n// servers at drain time and every task fails CI (2026-11-03). Acquired\n// BEFORE drainScratchPorts so a reclaimed occupant is definitionally stale.\n// Main process only: workers load this config too, but the main process\n// already holds the lock (workers would see a foreign holder PID and wait).\n// Released in global-teardown.js; a crashed holder is detected by PID\n// liveness on the next acquire. The\\n  // `load` gate hangs when slow subresources (Google Fonts CDN, build-badge\\n  // fetch, model-discovery warnings) stall under sustained suite load — the\\n  // tail tests timed out here after minutes of green runs. Readiness is still\\n  // gated explicitly below (title + h1 + Orchestrator button), and scan()\\n  // additionally waits for fonts + build badge before measuring.\\n  await page.goto(APP_URL, { waitUntil: \\\"domcontentloaded\\\" });\\n  // Tail-of-suite runs see multi-second shell renders under sustained\\n  // vite/API load (blank-page flakes at the default 5 s budget), so the\\n  // readiness gate carries the same 30 s budget as the tail test bodies.\\n  await expect(page).toHaveTitle(/Kainbain/, { timeout: 30000 });\\n  // The app shell must be rendered: brand heading + primary navigation.\\n  await expect(page.locator(\\\"h1\\\")).toContainText(\\\"KAINBAIN\\\", { timeout: 30000 });\\n  await expect(page.getByRole(\\\"button\\\", { name: /Orchestrator/i })).toBeVisible({\\n    timeout: 30000,\\n  });\\n}\",\"path\":\"canary-e2e/tests/accessibility.spec.js\",\"replace\":\"// Local readiness (NOT the shared waitForAppReady): the axe scans gate on the\\n// rendered app shell — brand heading + primary navigation — rather than the\\n// project selector, so the scan target is fully painted before measuring.\\nasync function waitForAppShellOnce(page) {\\n  // Most calls land here straight after a reload of this same URL (or with\\n  // the page already on it from beforeEach): re-navigating would abort the\\n  // just-issued module burst and fire a second one, doubling vite/browser\\n  // pressure for an identical load. Only navigate when we are elsewhere\\n  // (fresh about:blank page, or a deep link another step left behind).\\n  if (!page.url().startsWith(APP_URL)) {\\n    // Resilience: wait for commit/DOM instead of the full `load` event. The\\n    // `load` gate hangs when slow subresources (Google Fonts CDN, build-badge\\n    // fetch, model-discovery warnings) stall under sustained suite load — the\\n    // tail tests timed out here after minutes of green runs. Readiness is still\\n    // gated explicitly below (title + h1 + Orchestrator button), and scan()\\n    // additionally waits for fonts + build badge before measuring.\\n    await page.goto(APP_URL, { waitUntil: \\\"domcontentloaded\\\" });\\n  }\\n  await expect(page).toHaveTitle(/Kainbain/, { timeout: 15000 });\\n  // The app shell must be rendered: brand heading + primary navigation.\\n  await expect(page.locator(\\\"h1\\\")).toContainText(\\\"KAINBAIN\\\", { timeout: 15000 });\\n  await expect(page.getByRole(\\\"button\\\", { name: /Orchestrator/i })).toBeVisible({\\n    timeout: 15000,\\n  });\\n}\\n\\nasync function waitForAppShell(page) {\\n  try {\\n    await waitForAppShellOnce(page);\\n  } catch (err) {\\n    // Mid-suite resource-exhaustion windows (net::ERR_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES\\n    // across the module burst, root never mounts) leave a blank shell that a\\n    // longer wait cannot heal — the failed loads must be re-issued. One\\n    // bounded reload+retry; a genuinely broken shell fails twice and stays\\n    // red. The file-wide 120 s timeout below gives the retry room to land.\\n    await page.reload({ waitUntil: \\\"domcontentloaded\\\" });\\n    await waitForAppShellOnce(page);\\n  }\\n}\"}","output":"edited\nchanged lines: lines 41-61\n--- original\n+++ updated\n@@\n-// Local readiness (NOT the shared waitForAppReady): the axe scans gate on the\n-// rendered app shell — brand heading + primary navigation — rather than the\n-// project selector, so the scan target is fully painted before measuring.\n-async function waitForAppShell(page) {\n-  // Resilience: wait for commit/DOM instead of the full `load` event. directory fields show effective\n9|defaults instead of blank inputs; model selection toggles runner-advertised\n10|models instead of free text; the operator can re-kick model detection; and the\n11|operator can trigger a runner update from the page — plus the further refinements\n12|in Phase 6.\n13|\n14|## Success Criteria\n15|\n16|- Clicking anywhere on a roster row (mouse or keyboard) selects that runner;\n17|  selection still works with screen readers and keeps existing test ids.\n18|- Directory fields display the runner's effective folders on first view with no\n19|  typing, and saving is a single explicit save (no double-click confirm dance\n20|  unless a destructive consequence remains).\n21|- Models render as toggles over the union of advertised and allowlisted ids,\n22|  with a way to add an id the runner under-reports and a reset-to-advertised path.\n23|- A \"Re-detect models\" control asks the runner to re-run discovery and the UI\n24|  reflects the fresh list without a page reload.\n25|- An \"Update now\" control is offered exactly when an update is available and\n26|  causes an idle runner to update; a busy runner queues safely and the UI shows\n27|  progress/failure.\n28|- `npm run test:unit` and `npm run lint` pass; new behaviour has committed tests\n29|  beside the existing suites; user-facing docs updated.\n30|\n31|## Context and evidence\n32|\n33|- Page today: `frontend/src/components/settings/RunnerConfigurationSection.jsx`\n34|  (1040 lines, single component). Only the name `<button>` selects\n35|  (lines ~511-520); badges (`updateAvailable`, `belowMinimum`, update `failed`)\n36|  are display-only (~556-590); models are a comma-separated text input\n37|  (~854-911); directories default to `''` and the UI states they are \"not sent\n38|  to the Runner yet\" (~974-978).\n39|- Helpers: `frontend/src/components/settings/runnerConfigHelpers.js`\n40|  (`defaultRunnerConfig`, `advertisedModels`, `effectiveModels`,\n41|  `parseModelsInput`, `describeRunnerVersion`, `runRunnerAction`) — pure and\n42|  unit-tested (`runnerConfigHelpers.test.js`).\n43|- API surface: `frontend/src/services/runners/index.js` — list, monitor,\n44|  catalogue, config get/patch, approve/deny/revoke/pause/resume/skip. No\n45|  rediscovery or update-trigger endpoints exist.\n46|- Backend: `api/flow/runnerRoutes.js` has no runner-directed command endpoint;\n47|  the heartbeat response already carries a pull channel (`pendingSteers`,\n48|  ~line 279-313, ADR 0011) — the natural pattern for runner-directed commands.\n49|  Badges derive in `api/flow/runnerRegistry.js` `_public()` from heartbeat\n50|  facts plus `config.runnerMinVersion` / `runnerRecommendedVersion`.\n51|- Runner: `runner/modelDiscovery.js` (`discoverClaudeModels`, best-effort,\n52|  12h cadence, `MODEL_DISCOVERY_INTERVAL_MS_DEFAULT`); `runner/daemon.js`\n53|  self-updates idle-only and reports `updateStatus` via heartbeat facts; the\n54|  only forced update today is the 409 `RUNNER_VERSION_BELOW_MINIMUM` path.\n55|- Gap: the stage brief cites a grill survey at\n56|  `docs/tasks/8ded2dfc-0df7-424a-8c19-f2f8b78c0941/SURVEY.md` plus an idea file,\n57|  but that directory does not exist in this checkout — the survey could not be\n58|  factored in. Decisions below fall back to the task text and code evidence;\n59|  confirm with the survey owner before execution if it surfaces.\n60|\n61|## Key Decisions\n62|\n63|- D1 — One command channel for both \"re-detect\" and \"update now\". Rationale:\n64|  both are backend→runner nudges with the same delivery, ack, and staleness\n65|  problems; the heartbeat pull channel (`pendingSteers`) proves the pattern.\n66|  Alternative (separate ad-hoc endpoints per action) rejected: doubles the\n67|  protocol surface and leaves ack semantics inconsistent.\n68|- D2 — Runner stays authoritative for facts; backend stays authoritative for\n69|  operator intent. Discovery results and effective directories flow runner→backend\n70|  via heartbeat facts; operator intent flows backend→runner via pending commands.\n71|  No direct UI→runner calls (runners may be remote).\n72|- D3 — Directory defaults come from runner-reported facts, not invented\n73|  frontend constants. The UI must say so.\n80|\n81|## Work Plan\n82|\n83|### Phase 0 — Research spikes (first; unblock everything)\n84|\n85|- Step 0.1 — Survey recovery. Output: ADR-style note\n94|  under `docs/adr/` or the task dir; must be reviewed before Phase 3.\n95|- Step 0.3 — Directory-defaults spike. Uses the endpoint from Phase 3.2\n169|  via `frontend/src/services/runners/index.js`.\n170|- Step 5.3 — Polling/refresh: after enqueue, re-fetch the record on a short\n171|  bounded poll until ack/terminal state; no endless spinners.\n172|\n173|### Phase 6 — Own refinements (small, each independently shippable)\n174|\n175|- Per-control busy states: replace the global `busyKey` disable-everything\n176|  with per-action pending flags so one save does not freeze the whole panel.\n177|- Stale-runner honesty: when facts are old, badge rows \"last seen Xm ago\" so\n178|  toggles/commands are read with the right scepticism.\n179|- Empty states: no advertised models / no harnesses guidance already exists —\n180|  extend with \"Re-detect\" hint linkage.\n181|- Copy pass: remove \"not sent to the Runner yet\" wording once Phase 4 lands;\n182|  document the idle-only update semantics inline.\n183|- Keyboard/focus audit of the whole section after the split.\n184|\n185|## Validation Plan\n186|\n187|- Per phase: run the touched suites — frontend\n188|  (`npm run test --prefix frontend -- <file>` for the section + helpers\n189|  tests), backend (`npm run test --prefix api -- runnerRegistry runnerRoutes`),\n190|  runner (daemon/modelDiscovery tests). Full gate before done:\n191|  `npm run test:unit` and `npm run lint` from the repo root.\n192|- Contract checks: new endpoints covered by API tests asserting status codes,\n193|  fail-closed unknown commands, and no credential leakage (mirror the existing\n194|  \"never renders credential values\" test).\n195|- Manual/UI: exercise the page through the headless screenshot tool\n196|  (`npm run capture:screenshot`) against mock fixtures — roster selection\n197|  (mouse + keyboard), model toggles, directory defaults, both new buttons and\n198|  their busy/error states. No long-lived background servers.\n199|- Highest-risk validation: the Phase 3+4 round-trip (enqueue → heartbeat\n200|  delivery → daemon acts → facts reflect → UI updates). Cover with an\n201|  integration-style test using the existing fake client/registry seams before\n202|  calling the feature done; stale/offline runner behaviour asserted explicitly.\n203|\n204|## Documentation Plan\n205|\n206|- Update the `MARK:` doc comments on touched components/helpers/routes\n207|  (repo convention; `npm run docs:check`-adjacent hygiene).\n208|- Short operator notes where runners are documented (settings screen help\n209|  text + any runner README section): what Re-detect and Update-now do,\n210|  idle-only semantics, what stale badges mean.\n211|- Phase 0.2/0.3 design notes kept in the task dir; promote the command-channel\n212|  decision to `docs/adr/` if it changes the runner protocol sketch (ADR 0009).\n213|\n214|## Risks and Open Questions\n215|\n216|- R1 — Old runners ignore new heartbeat commands. Mitigation: capability/\n217|  version sniffing; UI shows \"runner too old — update manually\" instead of a\n218|  dead button. (Assumption: version facts are reliable; verify in Phase 0.2.)\n219|- R2 — Directory facts may not exist runner-side yet. Mitigation: D3 fallback\n220|  (\"unknown\") keeps Phase 2 shippable before Phase 4.\n221|- R3 — The missing SURVEY.md may contradict D1-D5. Mitigation: Step 0.1;\n222|  do not start Phase 3 until it resolves.\n223|- Q1 — Should Re-detect/Update-now be per-runner only, or also fleet-wide?\n224|  Assumed per-runner (matches page scope); fleet action is a non-goal.\n225|- Q2 — Can the double-confirm directory save be dropped entirely? A LIVE stack from a concurrent task verifies as a\n// scratch occupant, so overlapping suites kept killing each other's servers\n// and every task failed its CI stage (2026-11-03: no task passing for a day).\n// This lock serializes suite entry across checkouts, runners, and entry\n// points (gate branch, deploy.sh gate, manual runs): whoever holds it owns\n// the scratch ports, and any occupant found while holding it is definitionally\n// stale (previous holder crashed) and safe to reclaim.\n//\n// The lock is acquired at Playwright config load (main process only —\n// workers share nothing and must never wait on it) and released in\n// global-teardown.js. A crashed holder is detected by PID liveness plus a\n// max-age backstop, so a killed run blocks the next one for seconds, not\n// forever. text file `docs/tasks/8ded2dfc-0df7-424a-8c19-f2f8b78c0941/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`.\n1|# Runner config page refinement — Implementation plan\n2|\n3|## Goal\n4|\n5|Refine the System Settings › Runners configuration screen\n6|(`frontend/src/components/settings/RunnerConfigurationSection.jsx`, backed by\n7|`api/flow/runnerRoutes.js`, `api/flow/runnerRegistry.js`, and `runner/daemon.js`)\n8|so that: the whole roster row is clickable; directory fields show effective\n9|defaults instead of blank inputs; model selection toggles runner-advertised\n10|models instead of free text; the operator can re-kick model detection; and the\n11|operator can trigger a runner update from the page — plus the further refinements\n12|in Phase 6.\n13|\n14|## Success Criteria\n15|\n16|- Clicking anywhere on a roster row (mouse or keyboard) selects that runner;\n17|  selection still works with screen readers and keeps existing test ids.\n18|- Directory fields display the runner's effective folders on first view with no\n19|  typing, and saving is a single explicit save (no double-click confirm dance\n20|  unless a destructive consequence remains).\n21|- Models render as toggles over the union of advertised and allowlisted ids,\n22|  with a way to add an id the runner under-reports and a reset-to-advertised path.\n23|- A \"Re-detect models\" control asks the runner to re-run discovery and the UI\n24|  reflects the fresh list without a page reload.\n25|- An \"Update now\" control is offered exactly when an update is available and\n26|  causes an idle runner to update; a busy runner queues safely and the UI shows\n27|  progress/failure.\n28|- `npm run test:unit` and `npm run lint` pass; new behaviour has committed tests\n29|  beside the existing suites; user-facing docs updated.\n30|\n31|## Context and evidence\n32|\n33|- Page today: `frontend/src/components/settings/RunnerConfigurationSection.jsx`\n34|  (1040 lines, single component). Only the name `<button>` selects\n35|  (lines ~511-520); badges (`updateAvailable`, `belowMinimum`, update `failed`)\n36|  are display-only (~556-590); models are a comma-separated text input\n37|  (~854-911); directories default to `''` and the UI states they are \"not sent\n38|  to the Runner yet\" (~974-978).\n39|- Helpers: `frontend/src/components/settings/runnerConfigHelpers.js`\n40|  (`defaultRunnerConfig`, `advertisedModels`, `effectiveModels`,\n41|  `parseModelsInput`, `describeRunnerVersion`, `runRunnerAction`) — pure and\n42|  unit-tested (`runnerConfigHelpers.test.js`).\n43|- API surface: `frontend/src/services/runners/index.js` — list, monitor,\n44|  catalogue, config get/patch, approve/deny/revoke/pause/resume/skip. No\n45|  rediscovery or update-trigger endpoints exist.\n46|- Backend: `api/flow/runnerRoutes.js` has no runner-directed command endpoint;\n47|  the heartbeat response already carries a pull channel (`pendingSteers`,\n48|  ~line 279-313, ADR 0011) — the natural pattern for runner-directed commands.\n49|  Badges derive in `api/flow/runnerRegistry.js` `_public()` from heartbeat\n50|  facts plus `config.runnerMinVersion` / `runnerRecommendedVersion`.\n51|- Runner: `runner/modelDiscovery.js` (`discoverClaudeModels`, best-effort,\n52|  12h cadence, `MODEL_DISCOVERY_INTERVAL_MS_DEFAULT`); `runner/daemon.js`\n53|  self-updates idle-only and reports `updateStatus` via heartbeat facts; the\n54|  only forced update today is the 409 `RUNNER_VERSION_BELOW_MINIMUM` path.\n55|- Gap: the stage brief cites a grill survey at\n56|  `docs/tasks/8ded2dfc-0df7-424a-8c19-f2f8b78c0941/SURVEY.md` plus an idea file,\n57|  but that directory does not exist in this checkout — the survey could not be\n58|  factored in. Decisions below fall back to the task text and code evidence;\n59|  confirm with the survey owner before execution if it surfaces.\n60|\n61|## Key Decisions\n62|\n63|- D1 — One command channel for both \"re-detect\" and \"update now\". Rationale:\n64|  both are backend→runner nudges with the same delivery, ack, and staleness\n65|  problems; the heartbeat pull channel (`pendingSteers`) proves the pattern.\n66|  Alternative (separate ad-hoc endpoints per action) rejected: doubles the\n67|  protocol surface and leaves ack semantics inconsistent.\n68|- D2 — Runner stays authoritative for facts; backend stays authoritative for\n69|  operator intent. Discovery results and effective directories flow runner→backend\n70|  via heartbeat facts; operator intent flows backend→runner via pending commands.\n71|  No direct UI→runner calls (runners may be remote).\n72|- D3 — Directory defaults come from runner-reported facts, not invented\n73|  frontend constants. If the runner cannot report them, the UI labels the\n74|  fields \"Runner default (unknown)\" rather than guessing paths.\n75|- D4 — Model toggles keep the existing `PATCH /runners/:id/config`\n76|  `{ availableModels }` contract (allowlist replaces advertised; `null` resets).\n77|  UI-only change backed by the same endpoint; no new model-config API.\n78|- D5 — \"Update now\" respects the idle-only invariant (ADR 0012): the command\n79|  means \"update at next idle\", never \"interrupt a task\". The UI must say so.\n80|\n81|## Work Plan\n82|\n83|### Phase 0 — Research spikes (first; unblock everything)\n84|\n85|- Step 0.1 — Survey recovery. Confirm whether SURVEY.md exists outside this\n86|  checkout; if found, reconcile its answers with D1-D5 and amend this plan.\n87|  If not, record the gap as accepted and proceed on task text.\n88|- Step 0.2 — Command-channel spike. Read the heartbeat round-trip end to end\n89|  (`runner/client.js` heartbeat call, daemon heartbeat loop cadence, registry\n90|  `heartbeat()`, `pendingSteers` ack via `steerAck`) and write a short design\n91|  note: `pendingCommands` shape on the record, delivery in the heartbeat\n92|  response, ack path (facts echo vs explicit ack endpoint), TTL/staleness, and\n93|  what a runner that never heartbeats shows in the UI. Output: ADR-style note\n94|  under `docs/adr/` or the task dir; must be reviewed before Phase 3.\n95|- Step 0.3 — Directory-defaults spike. Determine the runner's effective\n96|  master/worktree folders today (daemon `workRoot`, project `cwd` resolution\n97|  in `runner/project.js`, CI workdir logic) and whether they can be reported\n98|  in heartbeat facts. Decide the exact facts keys and backend fallback when an\n99|  old runner does not send them. Output: decision recorded in the Phase 4 spec.\n100|\n101|### Phase 1 — Make the change easy (no behaviour change)\n102|\n103|- Step 1.1 — Split `RunnerConfigurationSection.jsx` (~1040 lines) into\n104|  focused units without changing rendered output: `RunnerRoster.jsx` (list),\n105|  `RunnerDetail.jsx` (right panel shell), `RunnerModelsEditor.jsx`,\n106|  `RunnerDirectoriesEditor.jsx`, plus a `useRunnerConfig` hook for\n107|  load/mutate/save/reload state. Keep all existing `data-testid` values.\n108|  Validation: existing `RunnerConfigurationSection.test.jsx` passes unmodified.\n109|- Step 1.2 — Extend `runnerConfigHelpers.js` with the pure logic the features\n110|  need (model toggle set-ops over union of advertised+effective; effective\n111|  directory resolution incl. \"unknown\" state; command-availability predicates\n112|  from record fields), each with unit tests. No network in helpers (keep the\n113|  `runRunnerAction` exception pattern).\n114|- Step 1.3 — Add shared fixtures/factories for runner records (advertised\n115|  models, update badges, directory facts) reused by frontend tests, so later\n116|  phases add cases not scaffolding.\n117|\n118|### Phase 2 — Frontend quick wins (existing APIs only)\n119|\n120|- Step 2.1 — Whole-row selection. Make the roster `<li>` the interactive\n121|  element (click + Enter/Space, `role=\"option\"`/`aria-selected` in a\n122|  `listbox`, visible focus ring); keep the name button's test id as the\n123|  accessible name. Add keyboard/a11y tests.\n124|- Step 2.2 — Directory defaults display. Show effective folders from\n125|  runner-reported facts (Phase 0.3 keys) as the field values with a\n126|  \"Runner default\" hint; operator edits override via the existing PATCH.\n127|  Remove or re-scope the double-confirm once the \"not sent yet\" limitation is\n128|  resolved by Phase 4 (if Phase 4 slips, keep confirm but fix copy).\n129|- Step 2.3 — Model toggles. Replace the text input with checkboxes over\n130|  `union(advertised, effective)`, plus an \"add id\" field for under-reporting\n131|  runners and the existing Reset control. Same PATCH contract (D4). Keep the\n132|  effective-list summary line. Tests: toggle on/off payloads, custom add,\n133|  reset-to-advertised, empty-advertised state.\n134|\n135|### Phase 3 — Backend command channel (the big piece)\n136|\n137|- Step 3.1 — Registry: `pendingCommands` per record\n138|  (`requestModelRediscovery`, `requestUpdate`), set via new\n139|  `POST /runners/:id/commands`-style endpoint(s), delivered in the heartbeat\n140|  response, cleared on ack/TTL. Unit tests for set/deliver/ack/expire and for\n141|  unknown-command refusal (mirror the `runRunnerAction` fail-closed style).\n142|- Step 3.2 — Routes + API docs: operator endpoints to enqueue each command,\n143|  returning a status the UI can poll (`queued` / `acked` / `stale` when the\n144|  runner has not heartbeated). Contract tests beside `runnerRoutes.test.js`.\n145|- Step 3.3 — `updateInfoForRunner` surfacing: ensure the record exposes\n146|  everything the buttons need (update available + recommended version +\n147|  last attempt state) — mostly already present; fill gaps found in Phase 0.2.\n148|\n149|### Phase 4 — Runner daemon support\n150|\n151|- Step 4.1 — Consume heartbeat-response commands: on `requestModelRediscovery`,\n152|  re-run `discoverClaudeModels()` promptly (bypass the 12h gate once) and\n153|  advertise the fresh list on the next heartbeat; on `requestUpdate`, run the\n154|  existing idle-only update path at next idle and report `updateStatus`.\n155|  Never interrupt live work (D5). Tests beside `daemon.test.js` with injected\n156|  fakes (mirror existing `updateDeps` seams).\n157|- Step 4.2 — Report effective directories in heartbeat facts (keys from\n158|  Phase 0.3) so Phase 2.2 has real defaults. Update `modelDiscovery.test.js`\n159|  neighbours only if discovery itself changes (avoid scope creep).\n160|\n161|### Phase 5 — Wire the new UI controls\n162|\n163|- Step 5.1 — \"Re-detect models\" button in the models editor (busy + success +\n164|  error states; refresh the record after ack so toggles update without reload).\n165|- Step 5.2 — \"Update now\" button in the detail header, shown exactly when\n166|  `updateAvailable` (with recommended version in the label/tooltip); disabled\n167|  with explanation while the runner is busy or below-minimum handling applies;\n168|  reflects `updateStatus` progress/failure. Uses the endpoint from Phase 3.2\n169|  via `frontend/src/services/runners/index.js`.\n170|- Step 5.3 — Polling/refresh: after enqueue, re-fetch the record on a short\n171|  bounded poll until ack/terminal state; no endless spinners.\n172|\n173|### Phase 6 — Own refinements (small, each independently shippable)\n174|\n175|- Per-control busy states: replace the global `busyKey` disable-everything\n176|  with per-action pending flags so one save does not freeze the whole panel.\n177|- Stale-runner honesty: when facts are old, badge rows \"last seen Xm ago\" so\n178|  toggles/commands are read with the right scepticism.\n179|- Empty states: no advertised models / no harnesses guidance already exists —\n180|  extend with \"Re-detect\" hint linkage.\n181|- Copy pass: remove \"not sent to the Runner yet\" wording once Phase 4 lands;\n182|  document the idle-only update semantics inline.\n183|- Keyboard/focus audit of the whole section after the split.\n184|\n185|## Validation Plan\n186|\n187|- Per phase: run the touched suites — frontend\n188|  (`npm run test --prefix frontend -- <file>` for the section + helpers\n189|  tests), backend (`npm run test --prefix api -- runnerRegistry runnerRoutes`),\n190|  runner (daemon/modelDiscovery tests). Full gate before done:\n191|  `npm run test:unit` and `npm run lint` from the repo root.\n192|- Contract checks: new endpoints covered by API tests asserting status codes,\n193|  fail-closed unknown commands, and no credential leakage (mirror the existing\n194|  \"never renders credential values\" test).\n195|- Manual/UI: exercise the page through the headless screenshot tool\n196|  (`npm run capture:screenshot`) against mock fixtures — roster selection\n197|  (mouse + keyboard), model toggles, directory defaults, both new buttons and\n198|  their busy/error states. No long-lived background servers.\n199|- Highest-risk validation: the Phase 3+4 round-trip (enqueue → heartbeat\n200|  delivery → daemon acts → facts reflect → UI updates). Cover with an\n201|  integration-style test using the existing fake client/registry seams before\n202|  calling the feature done; stale/offline runner behaviour asserted explicitly.\n203|\n204|## Documentation Plan\n205|\n206|- Update the `MARK:` doc comments on touched components/helpers/routes\n207|  (repo convention; `npm run docs:check`-adjacent hygiene).\n208|- Short operator notes where runners are documented (settings screen help\n209|  text + any runner README section): what Re-detect and Update-now do,\n210|  idle-only semantics, what stale badges mean.\n211|- Phase 0.2/0.3 design notes kept in the task dir; promote the command-channel\n212|  decision to `docs/adr/` if it changes the runner protocol sketch (ADR 0009).\n213|\n214|## Risks and Open Questions\n215|\n216|- R1 — Old runners ignore new heartbeat commands. Mitigation: capability/\n217|  version sniffing; UI shows \"runner too old — update manually\" instead of a\n218|  dead button. (Assumption: version facts are reliable; verify in Phase 0.2.)\n219|- R2 — Directory facts may not exist runner-side yet. Mitigation: D3 fallback\n220|  (\"unknown\") keeps Phase 2 shippable before Phase 4.\n221|- R3 — The missing SURVEY.md may contradict D1-D5. Mitigation: Step 0.1;\n222|  do not start Phase 3 until it resolves.\n223|- Q1 — Should Re-detect/Update-now be per-runner only, or also fleet-wide?\n224|  Assumed per-runner (matches page scope); fleet action is a non-goal.\n225|- Q2 — Can the double-confirm directory save be dropped entirely? Depends on\n226|  whether any destructive consequence remains after Phase 4 — decide in 2.2.\n227|\n228|## Non-goals\n229|\n230|- Changing dispatch/matching semantics, the update signature scheme\n231|  (ADR 0012), or discovery sources beyond the existing CLI probe.\n232|- Fleet-wide bulk operations; runner install/registration flow idempotent).\n9|- `commandResults`: map `command → { ok, detail, at }` holding the LAST ack\n10|  per command (including expiry), so the UI can show success/failure without\n11|  polling forever.\n12|\n13|Both persist in the runners state file next to `operatorConfig` (operator\n14|intent must survive a backend restart — a queued \"update at next idle\" still\n15|applies after the reboot). TTL expiry is evaluated lazily: a queued entry\n16|older than `RUNNER_COMMAND_TTL_MS` (24h) is treated as expired on read\n17|(`commandStatus`) and recorded as `{ ok: false, detail: 'expired …' }`.\n18|\n19|Supported commands (closed set, fail-closed on unknown):\n20|\n21|- `requestModelRediscovery` — re-run `discoverClaudeModels()` promptly and\n22|  advertise the fresh list on the next heartbeat.\n23|- `requestUpdate` — run the existing idle-only update path at next idle\n24|  (`maybeSelfUpdate` with `force: true`, so the interval gate does not eat\n25|  an explicit operator request). Never interrupts live work (D5).\n26|\n27|## Delivery\n28|\n29|The heartbeat route appends `pendingCommands: [names…]` (queued, unexpired)\n30|to the heartbeat response, next to the existing `pendingSteers` pull channel\n31|(ADR 0011). No new runner→backend endpoint: the runner acks by echoing\n32|`facts.commandAck = { command, ok, detail }` on its next heartbeats; the\n33|registry's `heartbeat()` consumes a matching ack (drops the queued entry,\n34|stores the result). Facts echo keeps D2 (facts flow runner→backend) and needs\n35|no extra auth surface. A runner that never heartbeats simply never collects\n36|the command; the UI reads that as \"queued — waiting for runner\" by comparing\n37|`requestedAt` against `lastSeenAt`.\n38|\n39|Only `active` runners accept commands: `pending`/`denied`/`revoked` have no\n40|heartbeat loop, so enqueueing there 409s with `COMMAND_INVALID_STATE` instead\n41|of queueing a nudge nothing will ever collect.\n42|\n43|## Operator endpoint\n44|\n45|`POST /runners/:id/commands` with `{ command }` → `202 { command, status:\n46|'queued', requestedAt }`. Unknown command → `400 UNKNOWN_COMMAND` (fail-closed,\n47|mirroring `runRunnerAction`). Unknown runner → `404 UNKNOWN_RUNNER` via the\n48|shared store-error path.\n49|\n50|The public record (`_public`) gains a `commands` block:\n51|\n52|```json\n53|{\n54|  \"pending\": [{ \"command\": \"requestModelRediscovery\", \"requestedAt\": \"…\" }],\n55|  \"results\": { \"requestUpdate\": { \"ok\": true, \"detail\": \"…\", \"at\": \"…\" } },\n56|  \"supported\": [\"requestModelRediscovery\", \"requestUpdate\"]\n57|}\n58|```\n59|\n60|`supported` is the intersection of the backend's closed set with the runner's\n61|advertised `facts.commands` (see below), so the UI can distinguish \"runner too\n62|old\" from \"command failed\".\n63|\n64|## Runner capability advertisement (R1)\n65|\n66|Old runners ignore unknown heartbeat-response keys, so delivery is safe — but\n67|the UI must not offer a dead button. New daemons advertise\n68|`facts.commands = ['requestModelRediscovery', 'requestUpdate']` (a\n69|`SUPPORTED_RUNNER_COMMANDS` const in `runner/daemon.js`, emitted by\n70|`factsFor`). The registry reports `supported` per record; when a command is\n71|not in `supported`, the UI shows \"update the runner\" guidance instead of the\n72|button. Facts-based (not version-based) so no version bump or semver\n73|window is needed, and hand-rolled runners can opt in by echoing the key.\n74|\n75|## Runner consumption points\n76|\n77|- `deliverSteers` (every heartbeat pull cycle): after the steer pass, consume\n78|  `beat.pendingCommands` — rediscovery runs inline (prompt, best-effort, then\n79|  acked on the NEXT heartbeat via `state.commandAck`, since the ack rides\n80|  facts); update sets `state.updateRequested = true` for the idle branch.\n81|- `joinAndHeartbeat`'s first heartbeat: same consumption, so a command queued\n82|  while the runner was down acts on boot.\n83|- Dispatch-loop idle branch: when `state.updateRequested` is set, run\n84|  `maybeSelfUpdate({ force: true })` at that idle point, then clear the flag\n85|  and stage the ack. Single-assignment mode honors the flag once after the\n86|  assignment completes (its only idle point).\n87|- Pinned models (`config.models`/`config.model` set): discovery would change\n88|  nothing (pins always win in `resolveAdvertisedModels`), so rediscovery acks\n89|  `{ ok: true, detail: 'models pinned; discovery skipped' }` without probing.\n90|\n91|Ack staging: `factsFor` spreads `state.commandAck` into facts when present;\n92|each staged ack is consumed by exactly one registry heartbeat (the registry\n93|clears the queue entry, and the daemon clears `state.commandAck` after the\n94|heartbeat that carried it — tracked by keeping the ack until a heartbeat\n95|round-trip completes, then dropping it)."}},{"id":16,"ts":"2026-11-03T21:39:37.123Z","feed":"tools","feeds":["tools"],"kind":"tool","turn":1,"text":"[RESULT] Read text file `docs/tasks/8ded2dfc-0df7-424a-8c19-f2f8b78c0941/phase0-survey-reconciliation.md`. 1|# Phase 0.1 — Survey reconciliation 2| 3|`SURVEY.md` (round 1, generated 2026-11-02T09:56:00Z) exists in this task dir, 4|but its `answers` object is empty — no round was ever answered. (2026-11-03)\n4|**Date:** 2026-11-03\n5|**Task:** Runner config page refinement (Settings › Runners: Re-detect models, Update now)\n6|**Amends:** `docs/adr/0009-runner-protocol-sketch.md` (adds a backend→Runner step), `docs/adr/0011-runner-steering.md` (reuses its pull-channel pattern)\n7|**Design note:** `docs/tasks/8ded2dfc-0df7-424a-8c19-f2f8b78c0941/phase0-command-channel-design.md`\n8|\n9|## Context\n10|\n11|The Runners settings screen needs two operator-initiated nudges: re-run\n12|model discovery now, and self-update at the next idle point. Both are\n13|backend→Runner messages, and the protocol has no such step — everything\n14|flows Runner→backend except steers, which ride the heartbeat response\n15|(ADR 0011) but are fenced to a live execution, which commands are not.\n16|\n17|## Decision\n18|\n19|- **One command channel for both nudges (D1).** `POST /runners/:id/commands`\n20|  with `{ command }` queues one entry per command name (re-requesting\n21|  refreshes it; idempotent). Unknown commands 400 `UNKNOWN_COMMAND`\n22|  (fail-closed); unknown Runners 404; non-`active` Runners 409\n23|  `COMMAND_INVALID_STATE` (a Runner that never heartbeats can never\n24|  collect the nudge, so nothing is queued for it).\n25|- **Delivery on the heartbeat pull channel, peek-until-ack.** The\n26|  heartbeat response carries `pendingCommands: [names…]` until the\n27|  Runner confirms. Entries clear only on ack or TTL expiry (24h, recorded\n28|  as an `expired` result, never silent), so a Runner that crashes between\n29|  delivery and action still collects the command on its next heartbeat.\n30|  At-least-once: the daemon skips commands already staged or in flight.\n31|- **Acks ride heartbeat facts (`facts.commandAck`), no new endpoint.**\n32|  The registry records the last result per command (`{ ok, detail, at }`)\n33|  on the public record, which is what Settings renders as queued /\n34|  progress / failed without polling forever.\n35|- **Runner stays authoritative for facts; backend for operator intent.**\n36|  Discovery results and effective directories flow Runner→backend via\n37|  heartbeat facts; the pending queue is operator intent and persists\n38|  across backend restarts (a queued \"update at next idle\" survives one).\n39|- **Capability advertisement, not version sniffing (R1).** New daemons\n40|  send `facts.commands`; the backend intersects that with its closed set\n41|  and exposes `supported` per record. The UI disables the buttons with\n42|  visible guidance (manual update) when the Runner predates commands,\n43|  instead of offering a dead control.\n44|- **Idle-only update invariant (D5, ADR 0012).** `requestUpdate` means\n45|  \"update at next idle\", never \"interrupt a task\": a live execution\n46|  parks the request for the next idle point (dispatch loop and\n47|  single-assignment alike), and the UI says so. A Runner that stages an\n48|  update confirms its ack over a final heartbeat before exiting, or the\n49|  rebooted Runner would collect a redundant command.\n50|\n51|## Consequences\n52|\n53|- The heartbeat response gains one optional key; old Runners ignore it\n54|  (safe), and old backends simply never send commands (the UI falls back\n55|  to `facts.commands` and disables the buttons).\n56|- Redelivery races are handled daemon-side (in-flight + staged dedup);\n57|  concurrent heartbeats cannot double-apply an update.\n58|- Fleet-wide bulk commands are a non-goal: the channel is per-Runner,\n59|  matching the settings page scope."}},{"id":35,"ts":"2026-11-03T21:40:08.437Z","feed":"main","feeds":["main","tools"],"kind":"tool","turn":1,"text":"[TOOL] bash({\"command\":\"wc -l
